summary: Plan re-read after the split returned eight findings. Seven are resolved in plan v5, including a real security correction to which capability set the catalog is built from; the eighth, how the two runtimes name tools, was an owner choice and is settled as a neutral reference each lane translates. Recorded against the saved plan file rather than the draft, which differs only by the factory frontmatter that plan save adds. Re-recorded after the hard-overflow rule was folded into the plan.
gaps: The artifact could not pass plan save: no decisions_reviewed frontmatter and missing the required Problem, Scope / Non-goals and Acceptance Criteria sections, with Surface Impact omitting CLI/ops, UI and docs.
The roadmap criterion required descriptors for five binding kinds while the confirmed spec correctly names four usable kinds, leaving the story unsatisfiable.
The plan forbade any path in a descriptor while the spec permits a reviewed fixed operand to render verbatim, so either implementation strips approved shapes or the security claim is false.
user_facing true is wrong for a backend and prompt task, and saying no functional check is needed cannot override what that flag mandates.

'Build from the access snapshot' is too vague at a security boundary: the job has a person-filtered capability set and a broader snapshot-derived one, and the wrong choice advertises an ungranted capability as ready.
The plan hard-codes one runtime's tool name while the two lanes name tools differently, and the proof checked only one lane.
The overflow guarantee has no end-to-end owner: compilation truncates at both the section budget and the total prompt budget, and the existing callback cannot emit the required startup event.
The live check was weakened to two tool families while the spec requires zero pre-success failures of any tool.
The plan had no behaviour for the hard-overflow case where even the compact name-and-id list exceeds the total prompt budget.
contradictions: The plan forbade paths in descriptors while the confirmed spec permits a reviewed fixed operand to render verbatim.
resolutions: Plan v5 adds the frontmatter with every active decision reviewed and all nine required sections, with Surface Impact covering runtime, data, MCP/API, CLI/ops, UI, docs, security and tests.
The roadmap criterion is corrected to four usable binding kinds, matching the confirmed spec.
Plan v5 prohibits executable paths, hashes and credentials specifically, and permits reviewed argument operands per the owner ruling; criterion 12 asserts all three against a binding carrying each.
Plan v5 sets user_facing false, since no screen, component or styling changes, and states that in Surface Impact.

Owner-independent correction: the plan now feeds the person-filtered inheritedToolPolicy.semanticCapabilities from execution-phases-run.ts:183, not the broader snapshot set, with criterion 2 asserting a capability active for the app but ungranted to the acting person never appears as ready.

Owner ruled: the catalog carries a neutral tool reference and each lane translates it. Criterion 5 asserts the Anthropic mapping against the real projection and asserts the DeepAgents entry absent, so the gap is explicit rather than silent.

Plan v5 exempts the capability section from total-budget truncation below its compact representation, asserts the guarantee end to end through prompt compilation rather than the renderer alone, and defines a startup event payload of counts and shedding stage with no capability content.
The live criterion is restored to zero pre-success failures of any tool, matching the spec.

Owner ruled fail closed; plan criterion 6b now requires the run to fail before any provider or tool call with a redacted capability_catalog_overflow startup diagnostic naming the granted and renderable counts.
open_items: Extending the catalog to the DeepAgents lane is follow-up work with its own proof; its absence from the mapping is asserted so the gap is explicit.
The document edit contract and decisions 0108 and 0114 remain in the superseded draft awaiting their own spec.

rounds.question: Two follow-ups came out of this work. Queue them on the roadmap now?
rounds.chosen: The document edit spec (Recommended), The second runtime's catalog (Recommended)
